vscode.adopt-offer.monosmith-if-it-is-no: MonoSmith: {what}. If it is not what you wanted, undo it in one step.
vscode.adopt-offer.move-it-into-a-folder: Move it into a folder of its own so smith can manage it?
vscode.adopt-offer.must-be-lowercase-let: {stringify} must be lowercase letters and digits with words joined by single hyphens, starting with a letter (for example web-app).
vscode.adopt-offer.is-not-a-folder-smith: {stringify} is not a folder smith can move the project into: {why}.
vscode.adopt-offer.it-is-the-repository-: it is the repository root, where the project is already
vscode.adopt-offer.it-must-be-relative-t: it must be relative to the repository root
vscode.adopt-offer.a-folder-that-starts-: a folder that starts with a dot is for tools
vscode.adopt-offer.use-letters-digits-do: use letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore
vscode.adopt-offer.is-at-the-root-smith-: {manifest} is at the root; smith manages one folder per project and does not pick it for you
vscode.adopt-offer.unticked-smith-commit: unticked: smith commits nothing unless you tick this
vscode.adopt-offer.enter-with-nothing-ti: Enter with nothing ticked leaves the change uncommitted
vscode.adopt-offer.the-folder-from-the-r: The folder, from the repository root
vscode.adopt-offer.the-name-of-the-folde: The name of the folder in {key}/
vscode.adopt-offer.name: name
